newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at sixth consecutive record.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at sixth consecutive record.

text.p: Dutch shares closed up at a sixth consecutive record high on Monday after starting lower, led by heavyweight Royal Dutch but without much new focus in the market, dealers said.
The oil giant gained 6.2 guilders to 288.40 after weekend reports of a potential merger with British Gas, though Amsterdam dealers said they remained sceptical.
"It looks like it was mainly picking up American buyers, as it really got moving after the Dow came in," one said.
Strength in the heavily-weighted banking and insurance sector also kept th index buoyant, traders said.
The index perked up after an initial bout of profit taking to come close t its all-time high of 611.48 in the afternoon, before fading slightly into the close.
Supermarkets group Ahold was hit by a downgrade from buy to market performer by J.P.Morgan, shedding 2.00 guilders.
"When it is one of the big houses cutting estimates it's always a concern, but it usually settles down in a day or two," one dealer said.
Brewer Heineken also fell back, losing 5.70 guilders to 317.10. Traders said the market was quite negative on the stock with some selling pressure emerging.
Volumes on the AEX were "no better than reasonable", a broker said, with activity concentrated in the financials. The financial sector as a whole is tipped to outperform in the medium to long term.
With the market still technically in an upward trend, there was considerable interest in buying dips, the broker said.
Dutch chartists are still upbeat on the prospects for further gains, with several seeing the index targeting the 630.00 area after achieving the near-term target of 610.00.
